# C++ Testing

Curated by Skill Harbor: an agent-focused testing workflow for modern C++ (C++17/20) built on GoogleTest and GoogleMock with CMake/CTest. It teaches the red-green-refactor TDD loop, test isolation through dependency injection and fakes instead of global state, the tests/unit-tests/integration-testdata layout, and when to mock (interactions) versus fake (stateful behavior). CI guidance covers running a subset first, then the full suite with output on failure, plus sanitizers for memory and race diagnostics. It even tells you when NOT to use it (feature work without test changes, pure performance tuning), which is rarer and more useful than it sounds. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; assumes a CMake-based C++ project with GoogleTest available; sanitizer sections need a compatible toolchain. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
